title: Video Shows ICE Agents Punching U.S. Citizen Teens En Route to Marine Enlistment in Alamo, TX
excerpt: Two 17-year-old U.S. citizen teenagers were pepper-sprayed, struck repeatedly, and detained for nearly eight hours by ICE agents in Alamo, Texas, after they stopped to film an immigration arrest near an elementary school. Viral video of the incident showed an agent repeatedly punching one teen in the face.
content:
On September 11, 2026, two 17-year-old U.S. citizens — Luis Ochoa and a friend identified as J.C. — were driving to a Marine Corps recruiting office in Alamo, Texas, when they stopped to film ICE agents conducting a vehicle stop outside Santos Livas Elementary School.

  • Viral video of the confrontation showed ICE agents pulling one teen from his car, forcing him to the ground, and an agent striking him in the face four times. Agents also deployed pepper spray against both teenagers.
  • Ochoa told local station KRGV that he informed agents he was a U.S. citizen but was told, "I don't give a damn."
  • Both teenagers were held in federal custody for approximately eight hours before being released without charges. Neither was the subject of an immigration enforcement action.
  • Ochoa's mother said she spent eight hours without any information on her son's whereabouts.
  • The teens filed a police report with Alamo Police, which said it was forwarding the case to the DHS Office of Inspector General.
  • DHS labeled the youths "anti-ICE agitators" and accused them of obstructing a lawful vehicle stop, disputing the teens' account.

The incident drew national attention and renewed concerns about ICE agents' inability to distinguish bystanders exercising First Amendment rights from immigration enforcement targets. The teens subsequently said the incident made them reconsider enlisting in the military.
